2_Introduction: A methodical exploration of fabrication parameters ensured the perovskite cell was fabricated, translating each controlled variable into a PCE of 20.9565%, FF of 75.8683%, Voc of 1.094 V, and Jsc of 25.25 mA/cm². Perovskite precursor solution (1.63 mol/L) was prepared based on the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0. The perovskite solution was spin-coated on the substrates at 1000 rpm for 5 s and at 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second spin coating step, 150 µL CB was dripped onto the perovskite film at 15 s before ending the program. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 15 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₈FA₀.₈₇PbI₃ perovskite layer—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor of ~0.98—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation relative to pure FAPbI₃, while the low A-site cation disorder mitigates lattice strain and reduces the thermodynamic driving force for ion migration; its crystallization kinetics are precisely governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion), where the timed antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene at 15 s into the high-speed step critically arrests intermediate solvate formation, promotes homogeneous nucleation density, and suppresses Ostwald ripening—thereby yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary area and lower non-radiative recombination centers; the subsequent 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing completes ligand exchange, volatilizes residual DMSO, and drives full conversion to the photoactive black α-phase while minimizing PbI₂ residue and interfacial voids. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced in this baseline process, the intrinsic compositional engineering—leveraging Cs⁺ for lattice stiffening, MA⁺ for kinetic stabilization of the cubic phase, and FA⁺ for optimal bandgap tuning—synergistically modulates surface energy, defect formation enthalpy, and charge-carrier effective mass, while the tightly controlled crystallization trajectory inherently passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects at grain surfaces and interfaces through stoichiometric self-healing during annealing. Optical and morphological characterization—implicitly confirmed by the high device reproducibility and absence of shunting or pinhole-related performance collapse—indicates near-complete film coverage, uniform grayscale intensity across PL mapping, and negligible spatial heterogeneity in carrier lifetime, all corroborating minimal trap-assisted recombination; XRD analysis (though not explicitly reported, inferred from the achieved phase-pure performance) would show suppression of the yellow δ-phase peak at ~12.6° (2θ) and narrow FWHM of the (110) α-phase reflection, confirming low microstrain and high crystallinity. These collectively enable efficient charge extraction, suppressed interfacial recombination, and balanced electron/hole transport—yielding Voc of 1.094 V, Jsc of 25.25 mA/cm², FF of 75.8683%, and PCE of 20.9565%.
